name: AMD Instinct GPU server solutions via AMD's OEM and system-builder partners
region: Worldwide; AMD publishes a qualified-server catalog PDF and a partner logo list
notes: QUOTE-ONLY - AMD publishes no accelerator price list at all, so price_usd is null by evidence, not by omission. This is the best-documented OEM channel of the three accelerator vendors because AMD publishes the partner roster explicitly on the Instinct where-to-buy page: Advantech, AMAX, ASRock Rack, ASUS, Bull AI, CANCOM, Colfax Customized Solutions, Dell Technologies, Eviden, Exxact, GIGABYTE, HPE, Aivres, Inventec, KOI Computers, Lenovo, MiTAC, MSI, Nor-tech, PEGATRON, Penguin Solutions, Supermicro, Symmetric Computing, Wistron. That list is the practical answer to 'who can actually sell me an MI350X' - it is long, unlike NVIDIA's, and it is a real sourcing advantage for AMD. Featured systems AMD names directly: Dell PowerEdge XE9785/XE9785L (6U), HPE ProLiant Compute XD685 (6U, 5th Gen EPYC), GIGABYTE G893-ZX1 (8U), Supermicro AS-8126GS-TNMR (8U). AMD also runs a Helios rackscale solution (72x MI455X) as the flagship. BASIS: as with HGX, Instinct accelerators in these systems are OAM modules on the baseboard and arrive WITH the system - there is no retail single-OAM SKU from AMD, so any 'per-GPU MI350X price' is a derived allocation, never a list price. Access motion is 'Contact Sales' plus the OEM catalogue; cloud access is a separate route. EXPORT CONTROLLED (true). Regime: US BIS advanced-computing export controls (the Oct 2023 interim final rule, 88 FR 73458 - source sup-buy-bis-2023-advanced-computing-controls), which put datacenter accelerators under ECCN 3A090/4A090, added the advanced-computing Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rule, and extended Regional Stability (RS) controls to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5. For items destined to Macau or Country Group D:5 the rule applies a PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL; other RS destinations get a presumption of approval. Practical effect: which accelerator you can legally be sold, and which SKU counts as compliant, is set by destination and end user - not by the channel.
